Grading Rubric

There are 8 possible points on this assignment.

Baseline (C level work)

  • Your .qmd file knits to HTML without errors.
  • You answer questions correctly but do not use complete sentences.
  • There are typos and ‘junk code’ throughout the document.

Average (B level work)

Advanced (A level work)

Exercise 1. Read and filter data to get data only for the 100 largest commuting zones (CZ). You will work with chetty_top100 throughout this lab. (0.8 points)

# If you have not already installed the packages, go to your Console panel and type    
# install.packages("tidyverse")

# Run the code below to load the tidyverse package
library(tidyverse)


#read in the data
chetty <- read_csv("Chetty_2014.csv")

# filter for top 100 commuting zones
chetty_top100 <- chetty %>%
  filter(top_100==1)

# remove the larger data set with all commuting zones from the work space
rm(chetty)

Economic Mobility & Household Income Across Commuting Zones

You will explore the relationship between economic mobility and CZ characteristics: household income per capita (hhi_percap). The mobility measure that you will use in this analysis captures the probability that a child born to a parent in quintile 1 moves to income quintile 5 as an adult (prob_q1q5).

Exercise 2. Make a scatterplot with household income per capita (hhi_percap) on the x-axis, and mobility (abs_mobility) on the y-axis. (A) Describe the graph: what is the approximate range of the x-axis? (B) What is the approximate range of the y-axis? (C) Do you think there is a relationship between these two variables? (0.8 points)

#insert code here
ggplot(data = chetty_top100) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = hhi_percap, y = abs_mobility))

ANSWER: (A) 20000 to 60000 (B) 34 to 46 (C) Slight positive relationship (no relationship will be accepted)

Exercise 3. Use color to represent the geographic region (region) to your scatterplot. (A) What patterns does this reveal? (B) Describe the distribution of the data, by region. (0.8 points)

#insert code here
ggplot(data = chetty_top100) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = hhi_percap, y = abs_mobility, color = region))

ANSWER: We get a better idea of the differences between this relationship when we color by region. The south and midwest are much lower than the northeast and west. The northeast and west have higher hhi_percap and abs_mobility.

Exercise 4. Represent geographic region (region) on your scatterplot using shape instead of color. Compare the use of color vs shape to represent the region: what are the benefits and drawbacks of each? (0.8 points)

#insert code here
ggplot(data = chetty_top100) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = hhi_percap, y = abs_mobility, shape = region))

ANSWER:

Exercise 5. Going back to the graph you made in Exercise 3, which uses color to represent the geographic region, add another aesthetic to represent the size of the population (pop_2000, population from the 2000 Census). Describe any relationships between size and region. (0.8 points)

#insert code here
ggplot(data = chetty_top100) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = hhi_percap, y = abs_mobility, color = region, size = pop_2000))

ANSWER:

Exercise 6. Split your plot into facets to display scatterplots of your data by region. (A) Compare this split plot to the combined plot from Exercise 3. Are there aspects of the relationship between hhi_percap and mobility that are easier to detect in the faceted plot than in the combined plot? (B) Which regions appear to have a relatively stronger relationship between hhi_percap and mobility? (0.8 points)

#insert code here
ggplot(data = chetty_top100) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = hhi_percap, y = abs_mobility)) +
  facet_wrap(~ region)

ANSWER:

Exercise 7. Add information on the census division (division) to your graph using the color aesthetic. (A) What does this reveal about divisional differences in the West? (0.8 points)

#insert code here
ggplot(data = chetty_top100) +
  geom_point(mapping = aes(x = hhi_percap, y = abs_mobility, color = division)) +
  facet_wrap(~ region)

ANSWER:

Exercise 8. Create a plot of the relationship between hhi_percap and abs_mobility with two layers: (1) A scatterplot colored by region, and (2) a smooth fit chart with no standard error also colored by region. (A) What patterns does this illustrate in the data? (0.8 points)

#insert code here
ggplot(data = chetty_top100, mapping = aes(x = hhi_percap, y = abs_mobility, color = region)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE)
`geom_smooth()` using method = 'loess' and formula = 'y ~ x'
